label: 2026 Q3 (Jul–Sep)
asOf: after-hours price of $124.18 on 28 Oct 2026 (7:27 pm ET, StockAnalysis)
headline: AI contracts are growing, but overall growth is slowing: the market is starting to fear AI will eat software

points.t: Net new AI annual contract value grew 65% y/y and the full-year target went from $1B to more than $1.7B; AI deals above $1M grew 4.5x in a year.
Q4 cRPO guided at +18.5%, 2.5 points below this quarter; full-year subscription revenue raised by only $15M.
GAAP operating margin fell from 17% to 9.5%: $9.17B was spent this year on Armis and other acquisitions, mostly borrowed.

reaction: Stock: closed at $150.13 (−3.0%) on report day and fell to $124.18 (−17.3%) after hours. Several metrics beat company guidance; what fell was Q4: cRPO growth drops from 21% to 18.5%, and full-year revenue was raised by only half of this quarter's beat. An analyst asked directly “when will AI momentum turn into overall acceleration”; management's answer was 2027. Next-day close to be added. Consensus from MarketBeat: EPS $1.02, revenue $4.09B.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: Almost all growth came from subscriptions; professional services lose money because the company now sends engineers for free to help large customers deploy AI.

rows.why: Includes this year's acquisitions of Armis, Veza, Moveworks and others; management did not give growth excluding acquisitions, and an analyst said it was a “slight deceleration” organically. Non-GAAP subscription gross margin 80%, versus 83% a year ago.

Gross margin went from +11% to −20% (non-GAAP): free AI deployment support for large customers, whose value would otherwise be booked as subscription revenue, cut about 0.25 points in Q3 and about 0.5 points in Q4.

segments.note: ServiceNow does not report revenue by segment. Security and risk appeared in 16 of the top 20 deals, CRM and industry workflows in 13; US federal deals above $1M grew 30% y/y.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: ServiceNow sits at the very end of the chain: whether enterprises really pay for AI shows up here first. The answer is that they pay, but it has not yet made total software spending bigger.

items.w: Net new AI annual contract value +65%, and agent usage in production grew 13x in a year. But $1.7B is only about a tenth of roughly $15.8B of full-year subscription revenue, and overall cRPO growth has not sped up.
To get large customers live faster, the company provides deployment support for free and books less revenue upfront. Management says this is only for the “first wave of adopters” and won't last.

ServiceNow saves more than $1B a year using AI itself, and headcount dipped. Customers do the same, which pressures seat-based software: the same day Microsoft said paid M365 seats grew only 5%, with weak sales of standard suites like E3.

Capex was $91M this quarter versus $235M a year ago; the CEO stressed it has “no compute or capital constraints”. It uses the compute of cloud and model companies and formed the Control Tower alliance with Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS, NVIDIA and others.
This year's acquisitions cost $9.17B in cash, funded by $3.9B of bonds and commercial paper; no buybacks this quarter ($580M a year ago), and cash and investments fell from $10.1B to $7.0B.

extras.title: Why cRPO is slowing
extras.take: Management attributed Q4's 18.5% to four causes, mostly timing and accounting, but the market didn't buy it.

items.w: About half of Q3's beat came from early renewals originally due in Q4.
On-premise contracts count as revenue but not in cRPO.
Backlog with termination-for-convenience clauses is excluded from cRPO but recognized as revenue; about a 0.5-point effect in Q4.
A small drag on both cRPO and subscription revenue; the company says it doesn't affect revenue over the long run.

trends.why: Q2's 23% included acquisitions; back to 20.5% in Q3
Q1 is the collections season; full-year margin target 36%

valuation.take: At the after-hours price, the forward P/E is about 26x versus a five-year median of 54x; only 2 of the last 20 quarter ends were lower. A 4% free cash flow yield is not expensive for large-cap software. The market is not questioning this year's profit; it is questioning whether AI will eat the seat-based software business.

forward.title: Full-year free cash flow from guidance
steps: Full-year subscription revenue at the guided midpoint of $15.785B; professional services $327M in three quarters + Q4 at Q3's $118M → full-year revenue about $16.23B
× 36% guided free cash flow margin → full-year free cash flow about $5.84B
forward.note: Our estimate from company guidance, not a company forecast.

history.title: Against its own last 5 years
history.sub: Forward P/E (next-twelve-month consensus) at quarter ends
history.note: About 26x at the after-hours price, above only 2 of the last 20 quarter ends (this March and June), the 10th percentile; median about 54x. The multiple halved in a year as the whole software sector was repriced. The current value uses pre-report consensus EPS (about $4.77). StockAnalysis data.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.note: Q3 free cash flow was $0.82B, a 20% margin; Q1 is the biggest collections quarter, so quarters swing a lot. Stock-based compensation was $0.63B, 15% of revenue, plus $0.18B of taxes paid on employees' vested shares, and with buybacks paused this quarter the dilution was not offset.

calc: Price $124.18: 28 Oct after hours (StockAnalysis, 7:27 pm ET), close $150.13; shares ≈ StockAnalysis market cap ÷ close ≈ 1.034B, market cap ≈ $128.4B
Net debt = short-term debt $2.09B + long-term debt $5.44B − cash and investments $6.96B ≈ $0.56B; EV ≈ $128.9B

changes.before: $1B at the start of the year, raised to $1.5B at the May investor day.
changes.now: More than $1.7B, and the CEO says to “exceed that”.
A “hybrid model”: seats keep budgets predictable and usage pricing drives growth; the CEO said revenue per user could rise 5x. On outcome-based pricing, customers are “not asking at all”.
Free deployment engineers for large customers, booking less revenue upfront in exchange for faster usage growth; it says this won't last.

changes.before: Kept hiring in sales and R&D.
changes.now: AI saves more than $1B a year internally and total headcount dipped slightly; quota-carrying sellers grew double digits while roles such as sales operations shrank sharply.

items: Every revenue and profit metric beat the top of guidance; “this is ServiceNow's inflection point as the control tower for super intelligence”
Control Tower net new ACV grew 6x in a year; EmployeeWorks reached $100M ACV in under three quarters
Armis, Veza and Moveworks contributed $100M ACV in three quarters, all ahead of deal expectations
No compute or capital constraints; capex falling and free cash flow margin rising
When AI momentum will accelerate cRPO and revenue overall: only “2027”
Whether AI “eats” or “adds” software revenue: no data given

AI ACV keeps rising but cRPO growth falls below 18% for several quarters: AI is replacing existing seat revenue
